_strings.@@d130ef5b9035: Treaty conformity — DC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from DC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the DC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: DC's Form D-40 begins from federal adjusted gross income (D-40 Line 4 and Schedule I Calculation A are titled around 'Federal Adjusted Gross Income'), and DC's only mechanism for adding income back is Schedule I, Calculation A 'Additions to federal adjusted gross income.' The verified addition categories on the 2024 Schedule I (Cal. A, Revised 09/2024) are: (1) part-year resident adjustment, (2) income distributions eligible for federal income averaging (Form 4972), (3) 100% federal bonus depreciation / extra IRC sec.179, (4) discrimination award subject to income averaging, (5) S-corp deductions from Sch K-1 (1120-S), (6) pass-through losses from DC unincorporated businesses exceeding the $12,000 threshold, (7) 'Other ... items not subject to federal tax but subject to DC tax,' and (8) capital gains deferred on the federal return due to investment in a Qualified Opportunity Fund. There is NO line that adds back income that is exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty (contrast California's explicit Schedule CA treaty addback). Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and DC has no treaty addback, it flows through and is NOT re-taxed by DC. Therefore DC conforms (treaty-exempt income remains exempt). Source: 2024 D-40 Instruction Booklet, Schedule I Calculation A and line-by-line instructions.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form D-40 Line 20: 'Tax' — instructions p.18: 'If Line 19 is $100,000 or less, use the tax tables on pages 85-94 to determine your tax. If Line 19 is more than $100,000, use Calculation I on page 17.' Line 19 DC taxable income = Line 16 (DC adjusted gross income) minus Line 18 (DC deduction amount): 'Subtract Line 18 from Line 16. Enter the result; if a loss, fill in the oval.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 CHANGE — STANDARD DEDUCTION ROSE WITH FEDERAL LAW (rates unchanged): 'The standard deductions are increasing based on the federal law; beginning January 1, 2024, from $13,850 to $14,600 for single and married/registered domestic partner filers filing separately; $20,800 to $21,900 for head of household filers; $27,700 to $29,200 for married/registered partners filing jointly and qualifying widow(er) with dependent child(ren) filers' (New for 2024, booklet p.3, restated in the Standard Deduction section p.10). The rate table itself is the same one in effect 'for taxable years beginning January 1, 2022.' Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form D-40 Line 16, 'DC adjusted gross income' (Line 7 total DC gross income minus Line 15 total subtractions). Line 7 = Line 4 federal adjusted gross income (from the federal 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR) plus DC additions (Line 5 franchise tax deducted; Line 6 other additions from DC Schedule I, Calculation A); Lines 8-14 are DC subtractions (taxable state/local refunds, taxable Social Security and tier 1 railroad retirement, income taxed on a DC franchise/fiduciary return, DC/federal government survivor benefits, unemployment insurance benefits, other Schedule I Calculation B subtractions). A filer with no DC additions or subtractions has DC AGI equal to federal AGI. The engine then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction (Line 18 for a standard-deduction filer) to reproduce Line 19 DC taxable income, and applies the rate schedule to reproduce Line 20. SINGLE RATE SCHEDULE FOR ALL FILING STATUSES: DC publishes one 'Income Tax Rate Table' (booklet p.3, repeated as 'Calculation I/Tax Rate Schedule' p.17) that applies to Line 19 DC taxable income regardless of filing status; it is duplicated per status here. Married filing separately is NOT half of married filing jointly — every status uses the identical schedule. PRINTED CONSTANTS VERIFIED EXACT (re-derived for 2024): $400 = 4% x $10,000; $2,200 = $400 + 6% x $30,000; $3,500 = $2,200 + 6.5% x $20,000; $19,650 = $3,500 + 8.5% x $190,000; $42,775 = $19,650 + 9.25% x $250,000; $91,525 = $42,775 + 9.75% x $500,000 — each printed '$X plus Y% of the excess over $Z' constant equals the cumulative sum of the prior brackets with no rounding divergence. NO PERSONAL OR DEPENDENT EXEMPTIONS: the 2024 Form D-40 computes DC taxable income as Line 16 minus Line 18 only — there is no exemption line on the form, so this pack ships no exemption keys; test vectors use exemptions_count 0 and dependents_count 0. TAX TABLE MANDATE below $100,000: Form D-40 Line 20 and the p.18 instructions direct filers with Line 19 taxable income of $100,000 or less to 'use the tax tables on pages 85-94'; only above $100,000 is Calculation I (exact bracket math) used. The 2024 tables are built on $50 income bands, so bracket math may differ from the printed table by a dollar or two within a band (observed: $61,100-$61,149 prints $3,595 vs $3,596 at the band midpoint) — the filed form must use the table when Line 19 is $100,000 or less. DEDUCTION TYPE MUST MATCH FEDERAL: Line 17 — you must take the same type of deduction on your DC return as you took on your federal return. The shipped standard_deduction applies only to standard-deduction filers. Itemizers enter DC itemized deductions on Line 18 via Calculation F (full-year/statutory residents) or Calculation D (part-year): DC does NOT allow a deduction for state and local income taxes (state/local real estate taxes remain deductible), and if DC AGI exceeds $200,000 ($100,000 for a separate return filed by a married individual) the itemized deduction (other than medical/dental, investment interest, and casualty/theft losses) is reduced by 5% of DC AGI over the threshold. ADDITIONAL STANDARD DEDUCTION for age/blindness NOT modeled: if born before January 2, 1960, or blind, an additional standard deduction of $1,550 per checkbox applies ($1,950 if single or head of household) via Schedule S, Calculation G-1 (New for 2024, booklet p.3 — up from $1,500/$1,850 for 2023). When married filing separately, the spouse boxes may be claimed only if the spouse had no gross income, is not filing, and cannot be claimed as a dependent. Claim it on the form — this pack ships only the base per-status amounts. DEPENDENT FILERS: a filer who can be claimed as a dependent must use the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependent Filers (booklet p.20; 'An updated worksheet is available for use by dependent filers' per New for 2024) — an income-dependent amount (earned income + $450 when earned income exceeds $850, floor consistent with the federal $1,300, capped at the regular status amount) NOT modeled by the shipped fixed standard_deduction. MARRIED/REGISTERED DOMESTIC PARTNERS FILING SEPARATELY ON THE SAME RETURN not modeled: this combined-return status takes a combined $29,200 standard deduction and computes each person's tax separately using Calculation J on Schedule S (each spouse's separate federal AGI, additions, subtractions and deductions), then combines Lines 21-35 — per-couple math the engine does not reproduce. The engine's married_filing_separately models a separate-return MFS filer with the $14,600 standard deduction. REGISTERED DOMESTIC PARTNERS: DC allows registered domestic partners to file jointly (use married_filing_jointly, $29,200) or separately on the same return — statuses that do not exist federally. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE: DC's 'qualifying widow(er) with dependent child' status takes the same $29,200 standard deduction as married filing jointly (booklet pp.3 and 10) and the same universal rate schedule, so the engine's QSS -> married_filing_jointly mapping reproduces the correct tax. PART-YEAR RESIDENTS: must prorate the standard deduction (and credits) by days domiciled in DC divided by 365 (366 if leap year — 2024 is a leap year; booklet pp.15-16, e.g. 71 days / 365 = 0.1945 worked example) and subtract income received during the period of nonresidence — the shipped full-year standard_deduction amounts do not apply as-is to part-year filers. DC HEALTH CARE SHARED RESPONSIBILITY not modeled: Line 25 adds an individual-mandate payment (Schedule HSR, Part IV, Line 17) to Line 24, producing Line 26 'Total tax and DC Health Care Shared Responsibility.' The engine computes only Line 20 tax. CREDITS not modeled (they are credits against tax, not base reductions): Line 21 credit for child and dependent care expenses (federal Form 2441 Line 9c x .32), Line 22 non-refundable credits from DC Schedule U (including the NEW 2024 Line 6 DHCD Rental Accommodations Division housing provider credit and the Calculation K out-of-state income tax credit), Line 27 DC EITC (70% of federal EIC with a qualifying child; separate worksheet, max $632, for filers without one), Line 28 Schedule H homeowner/renter property tax credit (max $1,375), and Line 29 refundable Schedule U credits (including Schedule ELC, max $1,160 per child). ROUNDING: the D-40 instructs dollars-only entries ('Dollars only, do not enter cents'); the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches for the Calculation I computation.
